  "wf..", // z20 chair, back to the west; table post

input.summary:
P1 upper hall is NOT lit in the merged build: min 0, 24 of 25 floor cells dark. The designer's layout with the dresser and table lanterns gives min 9 on a scratch copy (no lock), so the design works, but it never reaches build.nbt.
Cause: room-13's layers() call is commented out, and runParts refuses any write into interior air the shell already placed. A test lantern at (25,6,17) was refused by that lock; I reverted it and rebuilt, and build.nbt is identical to the starting build.
Only room-13.mjs was touched, and it is back to its original comment-only state. No lamp is placed; the designer's "confirm only" premise does not hold.
left: Upper hall is dark in build.nbt (min 0, 24 dark cells). Lighting needs the furniture and lanterns to be able to land first.

The runParts lock refuses any write into cells the shell carved to air, including air (verified: lantern at 25,6,17 refused as [25,6,17,lantern,air]). The shell (shell-west.mjs house()) should leave room interiors unbuilt, or the lock should treat air as unlocked. That is a shared build-pipeline/shell change, outside the lamplighter's remit, so I did not make it.
Same root cause as the glazing part: 230 refusals on glass_pane over shell air (window and door cells at y2..3). Those windows are not glazed either. P3 dining room also refused 9 cells.
Only 1 of 55 room parts reports refusals; 22 room parts place 0 cells. Most room modules are commented out (room-13 is one), so the furniture layer was never really tested against the lock.

Once the lock is fixed: uncomment layers() in room-13.mjs (the designer's layout) and re-run the lamp check. The scratch copy at /tmp/lamp-scratch/scratch.nbt shows the designer's layout alone gives min 9 with 0 dark cells, so the two lanterns are needed only if the layout is the one measured; the lamplighter must re-measure on the merged build.

Lamp spots that avoid the designer's cells and the lanes (free floor at y6 over the y5 planks): (25,6,17), (22,6,14), (25,6,14), (25,6,16). The tool's top suggestion (23,6,20) is the designer's table post, so do not use it. Re-measure after the fix.
